recentItems.title: FDNY deputy chief on being inside the North Tower as it collapsed on 9/11
recentItems.description: Former FDNY Deputy Chief John "Jay" Jonas tells Terry Gross about what it was like being inside the North Tower as it collapsed around him. This interview was recorded in 2011.

recentItems.title: Lisa Kudrow on 'The Comeback,' AI, and watching 'Friends' since Matthew Perry's death
recentItems.description:
Lisa Kudrow is up for two Emmys for the final season of The Comeback, about an actress who will endure almost anything to keep working. She spoke with Fresh Air co-host Tonya Mosley about her character’s delusion and how the show has captured different eras of Hollywood. Kudrow also talks about a life-changing trip to Belarus, being a strait-laced girl, and watching Friends after her co-star Matthew Perry’s death.

recentItems.title: Casey Gerald says no accomplishment will fill your soul
recentItems.description: A decade ago, Casey Gerald was running a celebrated nonprofit, giving TED talks, and on magazine covers as proof that the American dream still works. Then he shut it all down and disappeared from public life. Now, in a new book, 'The Great Refusal,' he turns his leaving into an argument about the limits of the American dream. He spoke with Fresh Air co-host Tonya Mosley about why he ruined his reputation to save his life.

recentItems.title: Director of 'The Uprising,' Paul Greengrass, sees parallels to pandemic rage
recentItems.description: Filmmaker Paul Greengrass sees parallels between what we experienced in Covid and the aftermath of the Plague and the Peasants' Revolt of 1381. He talks about rage, rebellion and his new film The Uprising with co-host Tonya Mosley.

recentItems.title: 'Spider-Man' director Destin Daniel Cretton found his connection to the world at the movies
recentItems.description: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' continues to break box office records, after having the biggest U.S. opening weekend in history. Fresh Air co-host Tonya Mosley talks with the film’s director, Destin Daniel Cretton. Long before Marvel, he worked in a group home for at-risk teens. He says it's an experience that shaped everything he's made since then, and became the movie 'Short Term 12.' Cretton also talks about growing up in Hawaii, his tight-knit family, and how he started making movies with his grandmother's camcorder.

recentItems.title: Please don't ask Lisa Kudrow to sing "Smelly Cat."
recentItems.description: The TV legend spoke with Fresh Air co-host Tonya Mosley about why she has "zero complaints" about 'Friends.'

recentItems.title: Marvel cancelled 'Wonder Man.' Star Yahya Abdul-Mateen II has a theory about why
recentItems.description:
Two weeks after actor Yahya Abdul-Mateen II was nominated for an Emmy for his leading performance in the Marvel series Wonder Man, Disney announced the comedy would not return for a second season. Abdul-Mateen says he's still not sure what happened — but he sees a pattern in Marvel canceling Black-led projects.

"When you look at the history of those projects and when you put them all together, there's no way around it," he says. "It does not look good. It does not look like good business. And it looks like it's certainly not favorable to its Black creatives." 

Abdul-Mateen spoke with Fresh Air co-host Tonya Mosley about how he stumbled into acting, padding his early resumé, and working through his stutter.

recentItems.title: Colman Domingo was bartending not that long ago... and then his life changed
recentItems.description:
Colman Domingo was still bartending in his 40s, going to countless auditions, and on the brink of giving up when his life changed. Now he's nominated for two Emmys, guest hosting for Jimmy Kimmel -- and he's still reinventing himself.

He talks about doing comedy with masters like Tina Fey in 'The Four Seasons,' playing Joe Jackson in 'Michael,' and why he loves being in his 50s.

recentItems.title: Colman Domingo loves being in his 50s
recentItems.description: Domingo tells Fresh Air co-host Tonya Mosley why he loves his 50s, and how he's embracing his "truth-telling season."

recentItems.title: Jon Bernthal on grit, dedication & the acting teacher who saved him
recentItems.description:
Jon Bernthal often plays intense, violent, damaged characters, like Mikey from ‘The Bear’ and Shane from ‘The Walking Dead.’ When talking about himself and his characters, Bernthal says that it’s easy for someone who’s scared to turn into someone who’s scary. He currently stars in ‘The Odyssey’ and the new Spider-Man film, ‘A Brand New Day.’ He spoke with ‘Fresh Air’ co-host Tonya Mosley about how he went from being an angry young man to a disciplined, dedicated artist.



This video interview was edited by Adrian Connor of WHYY Digital Studios.

recentItems.title: Lee Sung Jin on the breakthrough that led him to 'BEEF'
recentItems.description: The second season of Lee Sung Jin’s Netflix series ‘BEEF’ earned 16 Emmy nominations. Set at an exclusive country club, it stars Oscar Isaac and Carey Mulligan in a story about class struggles and generational differences. The storylines of both seasons were inspired by real events in Lee's life. Before ‘BEEF,’ he spent two decades in comedy writers' rooms, often feeling alienated as the only Asian person on staff. “That's what people first thought of me when I first started – I was the diversity hire." He spoke with Fresh Air co-host Tonya Mosley about the years he spent masking to fit in, and the breaking point that changed how he writes.

recentItems.title: 'Once' Bitten: Glen Hansard and Markéta Irglová (2008 interview) | Fresh Air
recentItems.description:
Irish songwriter Glen Hansard died on Wednesday. In his memory, Fresh Air is revisiting a 2008 interview featuring Hansard and Markéta Irglová.

The pair won an Oscar for their song "Falling Slowly," from the 2007 film Once. Written and directed by John Carney, Hansard's onetime bandmate, it's a movie about two musicians in Dublin, writing songs about past romances and exploring the love growing between them.

This episode originally aired May 1, 2008.
